definitions.explanation: Having a sacred, awe-inspiring beauty or grandeur that evokes a sense of the divine.

examples.japanese: {神々|こうごう}しい{雰囲気|ふんいき}。
{朝日|あさひ}に{照|て}らされた{山|やま}は{神々|こうごう}しかった。
examples.english: The mountain illuminated by the morning sun was majestic.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{神社|じんじゃ}の{森|もり}に{足|あし}を{踏|ふ}み{入|い}れると、{神々|こうごう}しい{空気|くうき}に{包|つつ}まれた。
examples.english: When I stepped into the forest of the old shrine, I was enveloped in a sublime atmosphere.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Derived from {神|かみ} (god/deity). The repetition {神々|かみがみ} means "gods" (plural), and the しい suffix creates an adjective meaning "having the quality of gods."

USAGE:
Used to describe places, scenes, or atmospheres that evoke a sacred or transcendent quality. Particularly common when describing natural scenery, temples, shrines, and moments of extraordinary beauty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神々|こうごう}しい{雰囲気|ふんいき}: sacred atmosphere
- {神々|こうごう}しい{光|ひかり}: divine light
- {神々|こうごう}しい{姿|すがた}: majestic figure

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {神々|こうごう}しくなかったら
